**Hypothesis 1:**
This hypothesis introduces several specific details not present in the study's abstract—such as trace element ratios (V, Ce), specific stable isotopes ($\delta^{18}\text{O}$, $\delta^{26}\text{Mg}$), deformation and metamorphism effects, and proposed future analytical techniques (LA-ICP-MS, EPMA, U-Pb geochronology)—while omitting the central mechanism described in the abstract (silicate melts interacting with oxidized $\text{P-F-SO}_4$-bearing sedimentary rocks to generate $\text{Fe}$-rich, $\text{Si-Al}$-poor ultrabasic melts). Therefore, it is not the main hypothesis supported by the study.

**Hypothesis 2:**
This hypothesis accurately and concisely captures the core thesis of the abstract: that magnetite-(apatite) deposits form via the crystallization of $\text{Fe}$-rich, $\text{Si-Al}$-poor ultrabasic melts, which separate from silicate magma through interaction with oxidized sedimentary rocks. Every element of this hypothesis is directly supported by the abstract.

**Hypothesis 3:**
This hypothesis makes numerous highly specific claims—including a particular locality (El Laco), mantle segregation pressures and temperatures ($1\text{–}2\text{ GPa}$, $1200\text{–}1300^\circ\text{C}$), specific $\text{Pb}$ and $\text{Sr}$ isotope ratios, Paleozoic $\text{P}$-rich ironstones, quantitative AFC mass-balance predictions, and specific experimental parameters—none of which are supported by or mentioned in the abstract.

**Hypothesis 4:**
This hypothesis specifies unsupported temperature and pressure conditions ($\pm 800\text{–}1000^\circ\text{C}$, $\pm 300\text{–}500\text{ MPa}$), specific rock types ($\text{P}$-rich ironstones), and a proposed mass spectrometry study of $\text{Pb}$ isotopes. Furthermore, it states that $\text{Fe}$-rich immiscible melts interact with sedimentary rocks, whereas the abstract states that silicate melts interact with oxidized $\text{P-F-SO}_4$-bearing sedimentary rocks to promote the separation of $\text{Fe}$-rich melts.

VERDICT 1: REJECT
VERDICT 2: ACCEPT
VERDICT 3: REJECT
VERDICT 4: REJECT
